task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-10-06, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
A defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 120 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: defensive suppression of opponent H2-H1 change
team defensive trait stability across seasons
counter strategy best and avoid defenses
methodological_questions: Is a defense's effect on opponents' second-half minus first-half change reliable across seasons (split-half or year-over-year reliability)?
How much of H2-H1 variation reflects measurement noise versus a persistent team trait?
What regression to the mean and sample size are needed for team-season defensive effects?
Do derived play-type possession labels introduce outcome-derived label bias?
evidence_establishes: The retrieval returned no earlier study-family records for this question, so no historical findings are available from this project's record set.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether defensive H2-H1 effects are reliable, persistent, or merely noise.
Whether any prior analysis of this question was attempted, succeeded, or failed.
Whether the play-type labels or H2-H1 measures have been validated in earlier work.
own_inferences: H2-H1 is a difference of two noisy half-game quantities, so its team-season variance is large relative to plausible true-trait variance; the reliability of the defensive effect is therefore the central question, not just its mean.
With 30 teams across 4 seasons (120 team-seasons), there are at most about 90 consecutive-season pairs, and these pairs share teams across lags, so the effective sample is smaller than 90.
H2-H1 is strongly affected by score state (garbage time, intentional fouling, closing lineups, pace), so an unadjusted defensive effect may mostly reflect game context rather than defensive quality.
The 'best/avoid' counter-strategy framing goes beyond a reliability question; establishing reliability would not by itself show that a defense is exploitable or that a counter works.
uncertainties: No historical record exists, so prior empirical reliability values for this metric are unknown.
The exact variance decomposition of H2-H1 in this data is unknown until estimated.
Quality and completeness of play-by-play, matchup, and rotation fields for all 120 team-seasons are assumed from the data description, not verified.
The data_catalog was not consulted in this run, so field-level availability is unverified.
Whether 2025-26 partial-to-complete timing affects the data version on 2026-10-06 is assumed resolved, since both 2025-26 segments are complete by that date.

historical_effect.explanation: No records were returned, so the historical evidence neither supported nor blocked the question. The decision rests on the design constraints (sample size, score-state confounding, reliability requirement) rather than on prior results.

blocking_constraints.text: 120 team-seasons yield roughly 90 lag-1 pairs with shared teams; detecting a stability correlation near 0.3 is borderline, and small true reliability would be undetectable.
Score state, pace, garbage time, lineup changes, and opponent quality can drive H2-H1 differences and must be adjusted before any defensive effect is interpreted as a trait.
A half-game difference is a noisy measure; its split-half and year-over-year reliability may be low, which is itself the main hypothesis to be tested.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved, so it is unknown whether this question has been answered. The proposal should not be treated as answered by prior project work.

risks.text: With about 90 overlapping lag-1 pairs, power for modest reliability is limited; the test may be underpowered for the effect sizes likely to matter.
Selecting the most extreme team-seasons on H2-H1 and then reporting their later regression would overstate persistence; selection must be done on one season and evaluated on another.
Score margin, garbage time, pace, and opponent strength can mechanically produce H2-H1 differences that look like defensive effects.
Play-type labels derived from play-by-play points can make the defensive effect partly a function of the outcome being measured.
Using full-season or playoff information to define labels used to predict later halves risks lookahead; the design must use only information available within the period studied.
Testing several H2-H1 definitions, play types, and lags invites false positives unless one primary specification is fixed in advance.
If H1-H1 or first-half splits show similar stability, the apparent H2-H1 trait is a generic team or measurement effect, not a second-half-specific effect.
Rule changes, pace trends, and roster turnover across 2022-23 to 2025-26 can change the baseline H2-H1 distribution between seasons.
Most team-level defensive traits are weak predictors of within-game splits, so the prior probability of a reliable trait is low.
Split-half and year-over-year reliability of H2-H1 may be too low to support a trait claim even if the mean effect is nonzero.

design.estimand: Lag-1 year-over-year correlation (and intraclass reliability) of team defensive effects on opponent H2-H1 points per possession, after adjustment for score state, pace, and opponent strength.
design.unit: Team-season (defensive effect estimate) and consecutive-season pairs of the same team.
design.sample: Regular-season team-seasons 2022-23 to 2025-26 (up to 120 team-seasons; about 90 lag-1 pairs), with playoffs analysed only as a separate pre-specified secondary check. Use only complete seasons (2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13; playoffs complete from 2026-06-21).
design.power: Target at least 80% power to detect a lag-1 correlation of 0.3 using the effective number of independent pairs; report the effective sample and CI width, and state that a null result at small true reliability is not evidence of absence.
design.controls: Restrict to competitive possessions (exclude garbage time by score margin); adjust for pace, opponent offensive strength, shot distance and shot quality mix, starter and rotation stability, injuries, and roster turnover; estimate defensive effects with a mixed model using opponent and lineup random effects; estimate team effects from one season and evaluate stability on another to avoid selection bias.
design.falsification: Placebo: compute the same reliability for first-half minus first-half-of-prior-season and for random team-label permutations within season; the H2-H1 trait claim is rejected if its reliability is not clearly above these placebos. Also check that the effect is not explained by score-state or pace controls alone.
design.multiplicity: One primary specification fixed in advance (regular-season lag-1 correlation of adjusted H2-H1 effects). Secondary analyses (playoffs, play-type splits, alternative lags) are labelled exploratory with Holm correction.
design.decision_rule: Declare the defense effect a reliable team trait only if the primary lag-1 correlation has a 95% CI lower bound above 0.2, exceeds the permutation and first-half placebo reliability, and survives the score-state and pace adjustments. Otherwise report that the trait is not supported; a result with a wide CI is reported as uncertain, not as rejected.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular season and playoffs as available on 2026-10-06, with play-type possession records from [source] database built from play-by-play; record the data snapshot date and the 2025-26 completion timestamps.
